It is possible that he asked me to give him the number, but I also believe that there were other ways for him to obtain -- to obtain this number. In any case, had he asked me for -- for this number, I would have certainly given it -- given it to him. I am now thinking -- now that you've asked me, I'm thinking whether the two of us have ever been together with General Hadzihasanovic, but I'd sooner say that we were never together with General Hadzihasanovic. But there was no reason for us not to be together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I've neglected to ask you one other question about Dusina in or on the 26th of January, 1993. Do you remember if the person who replaced Camdzic as the commander of the 1st Company of whatever battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was a person named Vehid Subotic, who was also known as Geler.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think that the deputy commander of the company was killed together with the commander. And given the course of events, I believe that the complete unit left our area because the situation up there had been pretty much stable by then. And we treated this as nothing but an incident. And I believe that there is some very serious positions above Dusina and those were taken over by another unit. When this happened, the -- there was no longer a security threat for -- for the junction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know -- do you know -- when you say there were some very serious positions above Dusina, do you know what positions or can you be more specific and can you tell us what units of the ABiH, if any, were on those serious positions?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I didn't say a hard position. I did say "serious position" actually. What I meant was that when a unit arrived there, a unit which was capable of defending the entire sector, I believe that those were units on the strength of the 303rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, do you know the name or number or more precise information about this serious position?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I said "a serious unit," meaning a unit which was armed and better equipped than this detachment of mine. And as you well know, the hilltop above Dusina was where the line facing the village of Merdani started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know -- sir, do you know if that unit that you've referred to that was on the strength of the 303rd Brigade was the Ironworks Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: The Ironworks Battalion? Yes, there was the Ironworks Battalion on the 303rd, but I'm not sure whether it was them. I believe that it was a company from a battalion, but I don't know from which one. It may well be that it was that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us to the best of your recollection how many soldiers were in the 3rd Corps in 1993?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I don't have the faintest idea. I would need time to calculate that. I know that there were a lot of names and a lot of people when assistance was provided, when packages were given to fighters to enable them to survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's fine, sir, if -- if you're unaware of the specifics. I asked you that, sir, because earlier you told us spontaneously in response to a question put to you by the Defence that thousands upon thousands of your men were prosecuted. And I'm just wondering if you can give us a rough percentage or -- or be more specific about the thousands and thousands of soldiers who were prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I could speculate, but not within the context of 1993 but of 2001, 2, 3, since the prisons in Bosnia are still full of people who have been prosecuted for those grounds and some are still waiting to start serving their sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I specifically do not need to know about 2001, 2002, 2003. I'm talking about in 1993. And let me ask you first: Were you -- when you said "thousands upon thousands of people were prosecuted," were you talking about 1993?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: In 1993, no. I didn't -- I didn't mean that there were thousands in 1993. I was referring to the overall figure. And the Defence lawyer asked me about the position of the 3rd Corps when it came to respecting the law, and I believe that my answer was provided within that context. I was talking about the policy of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, my final question goes back to Mr. Vehid Subotic. Do you know that person who was also known as Geler? Do you know that person? And if so, what unit was he in in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I don't think I can answer that. I did hear of this nickname, Geler. I never knew that this person's name was Vehid Subotic. There was no such man in any of my units, and if you want me to speculate, I can speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, sir. How did you hear of this nickname, Geler? In what context? How did this person with the nickname Geler first come into your awareness?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I just wanted to be honest and admit that the nickname does ring a bell; however, I can't put that person in any context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saric. The Prosecution has no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saric, to my learned friend's question you replied that Zulfikar Bojcic was in charge of security. Tell me, please, did he inform you which of the judges were involved in this investigation, be it in the morgue or elsewhere? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this person was a judge or a prosecutor. In any case, Mr. Vlado Adamovic's name was mentioned together with some other names that I can't remember at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend also asked you whether you know who the commander of the 1st Company was, the company that was resubordinated to the Municipal Staff, and you said that you only learned that when he was killed. You learned that his name was Camdzic. To your best recollection, was Serif Patkovic ever the commander of a company in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I know that Serif Patkovic was one of the officers that had graduated from the military academy, and I can say with certainty that he was never a company commander. He was always at higher levels, in much higher positions in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To my learned friend's question, you answered that Serif Patkovic may have been a battalion commander. Was Serif Patkovic ever resubordinated to you in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: You mean whether I was ever his commander? Whether I was his superior commander or whether he was attached to my unit for the completion of a task?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that period, in January 1993, was the battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade and Serif Patkovic as its commander, was it ever attached to the Municipal Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. There was no answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also told my learned friend that this company very soon was removed from the strength of the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff. Can you be more specific? How long after the events in Dusina did this company return to its brigade?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: This company stayed for no longer than two or three days after these events.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In light of your answer as to what you knew about the investigation based on the information provided to you by your security officer, tell me, please, did the Municipal Staff at the time and later on in 1993 while it still existed, did it have the military police bodies or any other investigative bodies which could have carried out an investigation at the possible request of the military court?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My final question is as follows: Did an investigative judge or a military prosecutor ask from you personally or from somebody else from the staff to carry out any investigation with regard to the events in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just one short question to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you took the solemn declaration, you said that you had testified in a national court and you mentioned the name Hakanovic. Could you please give us an indication as to who this Hakanovic was.

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hakanovic was charged with having killed a certain number of Croats during the period of time that we are currently discussing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was that?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: In Dusina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what -- during what exact period of time?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: The same period that we are discussing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this person, was he a civilian? Was he a soldier? What was his status?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: At the time, he was a soldier in the military police in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And is this procedure finished? Is this trial finished? What do you know about the outcome of this trial?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe that the trial has either reached the second instance court or it is probably finished. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you know why they called you as a witness? What kind of testimony did you provide in this case?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: This trial is public, and I believe that I read somewhere in newspapers that some people from Dusina confirmed that that person was not there at the time, and I myself was called to testify as the commander of the Municipal Staff because the question put to me was whether he was a member of our unit or not and whether he could have been given a task in the area of Dusina from the Municipal Staff, a task of any kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, do you have any other questions for this witness arising from any of the questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saric, did you ever, either as a witness in that trial or from the media, did you learn whether Mr. Zvonko Rajic's wife testified before that court?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: When I was saying a while ago that -- a little while ago that somebody confirmed that Mr. Edin was not there, I believe that it was precisely that lady who confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what she said about Serif Patkovic?

utterances.speaker: JASMIN SARIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. I have no other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On behalf of the Chamber, I would like to thank you for coming to testify here in The Hague. We wish you a happy journey back home. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have five more minutes. I believe that you wanted to say something very briefly. As you know, we have to stop this session at 7.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you very much. I believe that it will take less than five minutes. The Defence would like to address the Trial Chamber with an oral request in keeping with Rules 54 and 73 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, requesting the Trial Chamber to reply to the response of the Prosecution with regard to the joint request by the Defence by which we requested from the Trial Chamber to accept legal facts that have already been adjudicated in other cases. This request is a joint request by both Defence teams, and it was submitted on the 20th January 2005. The Prosecutor's response was filed on the 7th February 2005. We are of the opinion that in the Prosecutor's response, there are several legal errors and factual errors, and we primarily believe that in the Prosecutor's response the Prosecutor is making reference to some of the decisions by the Trial Chamber that have been rendered by this Trial Chamber. For that reason, we believe that it would be very useful for the Trial Chamber to allow the Defence to reply to this response in which way the Defence will -- would hold the Trial Chamber to render a decision pursuant to our request. We would like to be given until 18 February -- Friday, 18 February to file our reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This is a matter that my -- that my learned colleagues have raised that is clearly a matter between the Chamber and the Defence, and the Prosecution will take no position on that. I did, however, want to alert the Chamber and my learned colleagues that today we did file a correction in -- in that our response contained a few -- I believe two or three typographical-type errors, and so a correction to that has been filed. That correction doesn't affect the substance of what we've -- what we've put before you, but I did want to alert everyone that there is a correction that has been filed today. It's a two-paragraph -- a one-page, two-paragraph correction indicating a couple of places where there were errors, in paragraph 23 of our original filing. I just bring that to everyone's attention so that the Defence can take the correct version into consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This issue will be discussed by the Judges, and we will render our decision on Monday. If I understood your well, tomorrow we will not be sitting because you don't have a witness. On Friday, the Judges have their Plenary Session, which means that we will resume on Monday at quarter past 2.00. What is the schedule for next week, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very quickly, Mr. Registrar, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Looking at the clock, we cannot discuss the issue of documents that you wish to tender. I believe that there are quite a few of them. If we do it now, it will take some time. The list of your documents is very important. And I believe that it can wait until Monday, unless you want to have them admitted en bloc or not admitted at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I will want to admit -- have these documents admitted. We can do it on Monday. I don't have that many documents. We can do it within five minutes, but if you think we can do it on Monday, we will do it on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll do it on Monday. Thank you very much, and I invite you to come back on Monday at quarter past 2.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of February, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
